title: Speaker-tailored neural speech recognition outperforms familiar listeners for a woman with global aphasia and dysarthria (single case)
summary: A CNN trained only on one patient's voice recognized 72.65% of her words versus 56.75% for 12 familiar professionals; lab result only.
account: A 34-year-old right-handed woman with right hemiparesis, global aphasia and dysarthria from a massive left-hemisphere hemorrhage at age 19 took part in a single-case proof of concept at the University of Messina and IRCCS Centro Neurolesi Bonino-Pulejo (Frontiers in Rehabilitation Sciences, 2026). A compact convolutional neural network inside the CapisciAMe voice-input communication app was trained only on her voice, using 1,120 utterances of 13 Italian target words recorded in 33 sessions over one month in a therapy room; utterances from November 2022 (day not given, so 1 November is used) formed the held-out test set. The tailored recognizer identified 680 of 936 test utterances (72.65%), against a mean of 56.75% for 12 rehabilitation professionals who knew her. No real-world communication use is documented.
purpose: Recognise the impaired speech of a person with aphasia and dysarthria so a communication aid can voice her intended words
system: CapisciAMe speaker-dependent ASR (compact convolutional neural network, cnn-trad-fpool3) in a voice-input voice-output communication aid
developer: University of Messina and IRCCS Centro Neurolesi Bonino-Pulejo research team (CapisciAMe app developed in Italy as a research tool)
deployer: University of Messina research team (therapy-room sessions)
segment: Adults with post-stroke aphasia and dysarthria

ratings.reason: General benefit without an event: the result is a recognition-accuracy capability measured in test sessions; the paper documents no use of the system for the patient's real communication.
General benefit without an event: single-case proof of concept with a 13-word vocabulary.

ai_role.statement: The personalized CNN is the entire intervention; its 72.65% word accuracy exceeded the 56.75% mean of familiar listeners, but the comparison used a 13-word closed set and the authors state the single-case design and limited vocabulary constrain generalization.
